1: No farms, no shops: Stone Age Brits had to HUNT for meat and GATHER berries. Hunter-gatherers came first; farmers arrived later.
2: 10,000 years ago: picture Britain 'pressing 1-0' and leaving Europe the first time, long before Brexit.
3: Trick wording: the Commonwealth has no power over members, BUT it CAN suspend them. 'Cannot suspend' makes it False.
4: The plague didn't check birth certificates: it killed about a third of everyone, so 'children and old people only' is the false one.
5: Henry VIII 'collected' things: six wives, a new Church, and Wales (Act for the Government of Wales).
6: Elizabethan + drama = Shakespeare. Think 'Shake-spear-ean England'. Dickens and Hardy are Victorian.
7: Autocracy = 'auto' (self) + 'cracy' (rule): one person in charge. Britain is a democracy, so autocracy is NOT a British value.
8: Think nature: the National TRUST looks after green places, FRIENDS of the EARTH says it in the name. Crisis = homeless, PDSA = pets.
9: Patrick's cross is a red 'X' (saltire) on white. Andrew's is a white X on blue; George's is the upright red cross.
10: SWansea = South Wales. Both start with 'S' and 'W'.
11: The Eve is the night BEFORE Christmas: 24 December, one day before the 25th.
12: Steve Redgrave ROWED his way to five golds in a row. Think 'Red-grave rows red-hot'.
13: Cenotaph = Greek for 'empty tomb'. It stands empty in Whitehall to remember the dead on Remembrance Sunday.
14: Tim Berners-Lee: the W W W man. 'Tim's web' went live on Christmas Day 1990.
15: Five freedoms, one trap: the UK offers freedoms and rights, but NOT free university tuition.
16: 1455: the roses started fighting 'at 14:55', just before tea time.
17: Three parliaments, three numbers: Scotland 129 MSPs, Northern Ireland 90 MLAs, Wales 60 SMs. Scotland is the biggest.
18: Coalition = 'co' (together): when no party wins outright, two parties team up to govern.
19: Debates are public: anyone can watch from the public galleries of BOTH Houses. True.
20: Pool and darts: the classic pub pastimes. True.
21: Brexit day was 31 January 2020: the last day of the first month of the new decade.
22: 16 for a 'meal deal': wine or beer with food, with an adult. 18 to buy alcohol yourself.
23: Canterbury = the Church of England's HQ. The Archbishop of Canterbury is its spiritual leader; the monarch is its Supreme Governor.
24: Civil servants must be neutral, so they can't run for office. True.
25: St Andrews = home of golf. Andrew is Scotland's saint, so Scotland's 'holy course' is St Andrews.
26: Youth Court for most young people, but the MOST serious cases go to the big court: the Crown Court.
27: Skara Brae on Orkney: a Stone Age village so well kept it still has stone 'furniture'. Think 'scary brae, still there'.
28: National Trust: 1895. 'Eighteen-ninety-FIVE, keeping old houses alive.'
29: Gentry = landowners who were 'gentle-men' with land, the new class after the Black Death.
30: Elizabeth I's dad was Henry VIII (and her mum was Anne Boleyn).
31: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote comic operas: The Mikado, HMS Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance. The others are musicals and plays.
32: Loch = Scotland. Loch Lomond and the Trossachs sit in the WEST of Scotland, near Glasgow.
33: The King is married to Camilla, the Queen (Consort). Kate is the Princess of Wales, married to Prince William.
34: Anglican (Angle = English) abroad, Episcopal (from 'bishop') in Scotland and the US.
35: Walpole was first: 'Walpole was the first to walk into the top role' (1721–42).
36: Pancake Tuesday is the party, ASH Wednesday the start of Lent: the morning-after 'ashes'.
37: Free TV licence at OVER 75: 'seventy-five, telly free'.
38: Sunday lie-in: pubs open at 12 noon on Sundays, an hour later than 11 am on weekdays.
39: Number 10 Downing Street is the PM's home; Chequers is the country house.
40: EU referendum: 23 June 2016. Midsummer 2016 = the 'Brexit vote'.
41: Kelly Holmes RAN to two golds (800m and 1500m) in Athens 2004.
42: England holds 84% of the UK population: more than 8 in 10 people live in England.
43: 2010: just over 62 million. (2005 was just under 60 million.)
44: County Courts handle the COUNTless everyday civil disputes: injury, family, contracts, divorce.
45: Holyrood = Scotland's Parliament in Edinburgh. Holy-rood for the Scots, Senedd for the Welsh, Stormont for Northern Ireland.
46: England = rose (as in 'English rose'). Scotland thistle, Wales daffodil, Northern Ireland shamrock.
47: Robert Burns, 'The Bard', is Scotland's poet (Auld Lang Syne). Burns Night = poems and haggis.
48: British film studios boomed in the 1930s, the decade of the big-screen golden age.
49: Belfast is Northern Ireland's capital. Dublin is the capital of the Republic of Ireland, a different country.
50: April Fool's Day, 1 April: jokes allowed only until midday.
51: Ellen MacArthur SAILED solo round the world fastest (2004). 'Ellen sailed on the Mac-Arthur ship.'
52: 11 a.m. on the 11th day of the 11th month (1918): WWI ended at 11-11-11.
53: Welsh cakes are like mini scones: flour, dried fruit and spices on a griddle.
54: The London Eye is on the SOUTH bank of the Thames, opposite the Houses of Parliament.
55: The monarch's 'A-W-E' role: Advise, Warn, Encourage. They don't approve or decide policy.
56: Constitutional monarchy: a King AND a constitution, with the King acting within the rules. True.
57: To settle you need two things: English language AND Life in the UK knowledge (this test).
58: Crick and Watson cracked DNA. 'Crick = click: the double helix clicked into place.'
59: Henry VIII set up the Church of England so he could divorce, after the Pope said no.
60: Lent is the 40 days BEFORE Easter, getting ready for it.
61: The National Museum (of Wales) is in Cardiff. The Tates and the National Gallery are in London.
62: No TV licence? Fine of up to £1,000: 'a grand for no licence'.
63: Big Ben's clock is over 150 years old.
64: UK in the EU but kept the pound, never the euro. True.
65: NATO = mutual defence: help each other if attacked AND keep the peace between members.
66: Small claims (England and Wales): under £10,000. Scotland and NI: £3,000.
67: Enlightenment = new ideas 'lighting up' the 18th century (Adam Smith, David Hume).
68: Magna = great (think 'magnificent'), Carta = charter. Magna Carta = the Great Charter (1215).
69: 1485: the roses stopped fighting at Bosworth, and the Tudors took over.
70: Exchequer = the treasury. The Chancellor looks after the economy and money.
71: Newton studied at Cambridge. 'An apple fell on Cambridge.'
72: Romans out (AD 410), Anglo-Saxons in. Vikings and Normans came later.
73: Bronze Age: around 4,000 years ago. Stone (10,000 years) → Bronze (4,000) → Iron.
74: Hanukkah, the festival of lights, falls in November or December, around Christmas time.
75: The Mercury Prize: best ALBUM from the UK AND Ireland.
76: Boudicca (Boadicea), queen of the Iceni, fought the ROMANS. Her statue with a chariot stands by Westminster Bridge.
77: Britain is an island nation: rowing and sailing are the classic water sports.
78: Forced marriage is a CRIME in the UK: a criminal offence, not just a civil one.
79: A dog's collar must carry the OWNER's name and address, so a lost dog can be returned.
80: DVLA = Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency. Vehicles are registered at the DVLA.
81: Social networks = Facebook and Twitter. The others are shops, storage or music.
83: Welsh Senedd elections every FOUR years.
84: After Thatcher came Major. 'After the Iron Lady came the Major.'
85: The mayor is the ceremonial leader of the local council (chains of office and all).
86: First past the post = like a race: in each constituency the candidate with the most votes wins.
87: Wellington beat Napoleon at Waterloo (1815). He had the boots named after him.
88: Scotland's top criminal court is the High Court (of Justiciary): murder trials go there.
89: Tudor rose = red rose (Lancaster) with a white rose (York) inside it: the two houses united.
90: Wales flies the red dragon, 'Y Ddraig Goch'.
91: Adam Smith, father of economics: 'Smith smithed the economy' (The Wealth of Nations).
92: The King is the ceremonial head of the Commonwealth.
93: Weekday pubs open at 11 am (Sundays at 12 noon).
94: Britain is strong in SPECIAL EFFECTS and ANIMATION (think Wallace and Gromit).
95: Gainsborough painted people in gardens: 'Gain a portrait in the borough garden'.
96: Eid ul Adha, the festival of sacrifice, remembers Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son.
98: Royal Ascot is in Berkshire, near the Royal Family's Windsor Castle.
99: Julius Caesar came first in 55 BC. Claudius came back in AD 43 and actually conquered.
100: Tolkien wrote The Lord of the Rings. J.K. Rowling wrote Harry Potter.
101: Minor criminal cases go to the Magistrates' Court (in Scotland, the Justice of the Peace Court).
102: Bronze Age tombs = round barrows: round earth mounds like an upside-down wheelbarrow.
103: Defence stays with Westminster. The Northern Ireland Assembly can't decide it.
104: Census 2011: Buddhists (and Jews) less than 0.5% each.
105: Torvill and Dean ICE DANCED to Boléro in 1984 and scored perfect sixes.
106: The anthem starts 'God save our gracious King'.
107: Radioactivity was discovered in France (Becquerel, the Curies), so it is NOT a British invention.
108: Churchill's first speech as PM (1940): 'blood, toil, tears and sweat'.
109: Bulgaria sided with Germany (the Central Powers) in WWI, so it was NOT one of the Allies.
110: Homeless charities: Shelter (a roof) and Crisis (help when things go wrong).
111: Scotland's flower is the prickly thistle, like the Scots defending their land.
112: Your TV licence pays for the BBC.
113: Wales, Scotland and NI use proportional representation. First past the post is for Westminster.
114: Commonwealth = 'common wealth': countries helping each other on democracy and development.
115: Christopher Wren built St Paul's after the Great Fire of 1666. 'Wren built the nest on the hill.'
116: Individual liberty is one of the five British values (democracy, rule of law, liberty, tolerance, community).
117: Mozambique joined the Commonwealth even though it was never British.
118: Nearly everyone in paid work pays National Insurance, including the self-employed.
119: Buying local helps your community. True.
120: The Cenotaph is in Whitehall, London.
121: Great Britain = England, Scotland and Wales only. Add Northern Ireland and you get the UK.
122: Bradley Wiggins was the first Briton to win the Tour de France (2012). 'Wiggins wiggled up the Alps.'
123: English has many accents and dialects: think Geordie, Scouse, Cockney.
124: Betting shops and gambling: 18 or over.
125: McEwan, Mantel and Barnes all won the Booker Prize, the big fiction-book award.
126: NI Assembly members (MLAs) are elected by proportional representation.
127: Contact your MP by letter or by phoning their constituency office.
128: Bill of Rights 1689: Parliament's rights, and limits on the king's power.
129: Isambard Kingdom Brunel built the Clifton bridge (and the Great Western Railway).
130: No: the British constitution is 'unwritten', spread across laws and conventions rather than one document.
